subject: UrbanHealth — residency for DR failover and subprocessor visibility

Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency for DR failover — quick clarification & list of asks

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week. UrbanHealth legal and security have a short set of questions we need to close before we proceed to contracting. High level: we must keep PHI-derived payloads anchored in the US but we also need a documented, time‑boxed DR/maintenance failover process that may momentarily route processing outside the US (e.g., to a cloud region in Canada or EU) for up to 72 hours in a true emergency.

Can you confirm the following detail points so we can include them in our DPA appendix?
- Does Redwood support an explicit "anchoring" statement that guarantees primary processing in the US and a documented transient failover window (72h max) with notification?
- If transient cross‑region processing occurs, what telemetry/audit evidence can you provide (timestamps, origin region, affected request IDs)?
- Which subprocessors would be involved in a cross‑region failover (we're particularly concerned about any APAC vendors)?
- Any standard contractual language you recommend for the DPA appendix and a short specimen clause we can circulate to our counsel?

I'm attaching our DPA questionnaire (UrbanHealth_DPA_appendix_questions.pdf) with a couple of redlines for context. Procurement will follow up with redline requests if the answers work for them.

Appreciate a concise response — legal is on a tight timeline.

Best,
Jamie
Director, Data Governance
UrbanHealth

Subject: Re: Residency for DR failover — quick clarification & list of asks

Hi Jamie — thanks for the clear list. I pulled in Marissa (product privacy) and Ben (ops) to make sure we cover the technical and contractual items. Answers below at a high level; I also attached a short runbook (ops_failover_runbook.xlsx) and a specimen DPA appendix language block.

High‑level: Redwood can provide an anchoring commitment and a bounded transient failover window for genuine disaster/maintenance events. We treat the US region as the primary processing locus when customers select US residency. Cross‑region processing is only used under documented failover conditions and is time‑boxed; we notify customers via email and through the Console incident banner when it occurs.

Telemetry/audit evidence we can supply:
- Per-request trace (request id, timestamp, origin region, processing region) for the affected window (CSV export)
- System incident record and timeline (start/stop times, runbook steps executed)
- Operator-run diagnostic logs filtered by request id(s) (redacted for operator information)

Subprocessors & APAC scope:
- Primary infra and control plane: AWS (us-east-1), GCP (us-central1) as configured for US residency.
- For transient routing we may use regional edge caches or replica nodes in partner regions (Canada/EU) operated by our cloud providers. We do not route to APAC unless a customer explicitly requests APAC pinning or an extraordinary global incident requires it; in practice that means APAC subprocessors would not be engaged for a US‑pinned tenant without explicit consent.
- Full subprocessor roster and activation triggers are in our standard DPA sub‑appendix; we can produce a filtered roster showing which subprocessors could be involuntarily engaged for a bounded failover.

Suggested DPA appendix language (summary):
- Anchor: "Redwood will process Customer Data within the US under normal operations. In limited, time‑boxed failover scenarios (emergency maintenance, catastrophe), Redwood may temporarily route processing to non‑US locations for no longer than 72 hours unless otherwise agreed in writing; Redwood will provide notice and audit evidence as described below."
- Evidence: "Redwood shall provide request‑level traces and an incident timeline within 5 business days of event closure."

Next steps: Ben has the runbook and can add the specific telemetry export format. If the language above looks acceptable, I can produce a DPA appendix draft for counsel review.

– Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Privacy Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Adding operational color from the runtime side. Jamie, short practical notes to set expectations for your ops/security teams: 

1) KV cache & inference artifacts:
- We have a prefix cache that lives in-region for latency; in failover we allow ephemeral cache warm‑start in the failover region to stabilize latency. Cached artifacts are short‑lived (TTL measured in hours) and do not alter custody of underlying customer data.

2) Data path and encryption:
- Customer payloads remain encrypted at rest and in transit. When we replicate ephemeral replicas for failover we use customer‑keyed encryption where requested (KMS/HSM integrations) — we can scope key residency to the US.

3) Activation & operator controls:
- Failover can be automated by policy (region outage) or manual by SRE on-call. We maintain a documented activation checklist (what we call the "bounded failover checklist") and require two‑person approval for any manual cross‑region activation.

4) Evidence export format:
- We can deliver a CSV with columns: request_id, original_region, processing_region, start_ts, end_ts, model_variant, anomaly_flag. We can also push the export into a secure S3/GCS share for you.

If UrbanHealth wants us to redact model debug traces further, we can agree a narrow set of fields to exclude prior to evidence export. Happy to jump on a 30‑minute technical call to walk through the runbook.

—Marissa
Senior Product Manager, Privacy & Policy
Redwood Inference
